newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise stock falls, Suez rises.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise stock falls, Suez rises.

text.p: Shares in Lyonnaise des Eaux opened 0.56 percent lower on Monday when they resumed trading after the formal announcement on Friday of plans to merge with Cie de Suez. Suez shares opened up 0.25 percent.
Within minutes of the bourse opening, both were trading lower, pressured by a drop in the market following a sharp fall on Wall Street on Friday.
Suez shares were 0.21 percent lower at 280.70 francs at 0820 GMT, and Lyonnaise shares were down 2.59 percent at 526 francs.
The CAC-40 index was down 1.6 percent at the same time.
The two companies confirmed on Friday that they had agreed to merge. Suez said it would pay its shareholders a dividend three times last year's payout.
The companies said they expected 1997 profit of at least 3.5 billion francs and aimed to double earnings per share in five years.

The chairman designate of the management board of Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux, Gerard Mestrallet, told an analysts' meeting on Monday that Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux expected 1997 pre-tax pre-exceptional profit of slightly over 3.5 billion francs.
